reviews.body: Thanks for picking this up! the approach makes sense. ran the suite plus some edge cases locally, a couple of things inline around other shapes Gemini's been reported sending and test coverage for them

Thanks for the follow up! a couple more things inline. also could you update the description? it still says deltas with an index are grouped exactly as before, but a new id on a taken index now opens a new call
lgtm! ran the unit tests and both openai node-integration suites locally (they fail on develop and pass here), plus a few out of order index cases, all good 👍

review_comments.body: m: this covers undefined indexes, but we can still get "index": null or index: 0 on every call, and those still get merged into one call. could you start a new call when a different non empty id lands on a taken index and treat null like missing? and could you add test cases for those two shapes?

could we also get a node-integration test for this? a Gemini style stream in dev-packages/node-integration-tests/suites/tracing/openai/openai-tool-calls/scenario.mjs (whole parallel calls, no index) so it goes through the real openai SDK, the unit tests call instrumentStream directly

m: the tool calls can come out of order now, index 0 call_a, index 0 call_b, then index 1 call_c gets recorded as [a, c, b]. 

Object.values puts integer keys ahead of string ones so index-0-1 lands last. the .sort() in the "later real index" test hides the same thing for no-index then indexed. could you key every call by a string (or use a Map) and assert the order in those tests?

l: thanks for adding it! ran it locally and the gemini case fails on develop, so it catches the bug 👍 we can keep it, but could you also add the same stream to scenario-chat.mjs? that one uses the real OpenAI client against an express server sending SSE, so the SDK actually parses the chunks

comments.body:
Thanks for the careful review. Pushed a follow-up commit:

- `index: null` is now treated like a missing index, and a different non-empty `id` arriving on an index that is already taken starts a new call (an `id` that is already known still continues its own call, and a delta with no `id` continues the latest call opened on that index). Four unit test cases cover null indexes, `index: 0` on every call, a fragment after a reused index, and a repeated `id` not splitting its call; three of them fail without the change.
- Added a Gemini-style stream to the `openai-tool-calls` node-integration scenario (two whole parallel calls, no `index`), with the expectations in both the recording-enabled and recording-disabled tests. The node-integration suite was not run locally (no built `@sentry/node`), so that part has only been syntax-checked; CI will be its first run.

This comment was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code).

Thanks, all three done in the follow-up commit:

- Order: tool calls are now keyed by string in a `Map`, so they come out in the order they were opened. Added your case (index 0 `call_a`, index 0 `call_b`, index 1 `call_c` -> `[a, b, c]`), and the no-index-then-indexed test asserts the order instead of using `.sort()`.
- `scenario-chat.mjs` now streams the Gemini-style tool calls (two whole calls, no `index`) from the Express SSE server, so the real `openai` SDK parses the chunks; the three `scenario-chat` tests expect 9 spans and check the tool calls with recording on and off.
- Updated the description.

The node-integration suite was not run locally (no built `@sentry/node`), only the unit tests (`packages/server-utils` ai tests pass) and a syntax check of the scenario, so CI will be its first run.

This comment was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code).
